title: This old-school way of investing money is better than ever — even in the age of AI and mega-IPOs
excerpt: The “golden ratio” for portfolio construction — 60% stocks, 40% bonds — works again, but with a few tweaks.
content_html:
MarketWatch

Sat, August 15, 2026 at 4:30 AM MST 5 min read

The "golden ratio" of investing is back, even if it's for different reasons than when it was developed.

The 60% stocks, 40% bonds portfolio has been declared dead more times than I can count. The reason was always the same — and it started with the 60%. For the better part of 15 years, the equity side of the portfolio came down to one trade: own the S&P 500 SPX and try not to get too clever about the rest.

Most Read from MarketWatch

  • I'm 63, a retired CPA with a $1.2 million 401(k). Do I need to bother with a Roth conversion?

  • My friend's mother died. Can she stop Medicaid from taking the family home?

  • The 'Hindenburg Omen' keeps flashing. Should investors worry about a stock-market crash?

  • Can I claim 50% of my husband's Social Security now — and switch to my higher benefit at 70?

  • Social Security recipients will get more money next year. Here's how much the COLA may boost benefits.

Anything added on top of that looked like a drag on returns. International stocks lagged. Emerging markets disappointed. Bonds, during most of that stretch, delivered returns similar to a bank deposit. Every diversified portfolio looked like a mistake next to the index.

But thanks to a few makeovers, the 60/40 is back — and better than ever.

The S&P 500 was built to represent a broad basket of the market. That's no longer true: A limited number of companies now drive most of its returns as they fuel the buildout of artificial intelligence, and an even smaller handful "chip" in the rest — pun intended.

Meanwhile, the number of publicly listed U.S. companies has fallen by roughly half since the mid-1990s, from close to 8,000 to under 5,000 today.

The companies that used to define an index, going public early in their growth, now opt to wait. Instead, they stay private — with many going public well after they've already achieved hockey-stick growth, leaving public investors chasing a ship that has already left the port.

This summer's SpaceX SPCX initial public offering was the cleanest illustration of this shift. The company went public in June at a valuation north of $2 trillion, after spending more than two decades in private hands. That is not an anomaly. It's an established pattern.

The median age of a U.S. technology company at IPO has roughly doubled since 2000, from about six years to 12. Companies that once needed public markets to fund their next stage of growth now have no shortage of private capital willing to fund growth, and no shortage of reasons to avoid the quarterly scrutiny that comes with public ownership.

content_html_zh:
市场观察

2026 年 8 月 15 日星期六凌晨 4:30（MST） 阅读 5 分钟

投资的“黄金比例”又回来了，尽管其原因与它产生时不同。

60% 股票、40% 债券的投资组合已经被宣布死亡的次数多得我数不清了。 原因总是一样的——都是从 60% 开始的。 在 15 年的大部分时间里，投资组合的股票方面归结为一项交易：持有 S&P 500 SPX，并尽量不要对其他股票过于聪明。

大多数阅读来自 MarketWatch

  • 我今年 63 岁，是一名退休注册会计师，拥有 120 万美元的 401(k) 资金。 我需要费心进行罗斯转换吗？
  • 我朋友的母亲去世了。 她能阻止医疗补助将家人带回家吗？
  • “兴登堡预兆”不断闪烁。 投资者应该担心股市崩盘吗？
  • 我现在可以领取我丈夫社会保障金的 50%，并在 70 岁时转到更高的福利金吗？
  • 社会保障领取者明年将获得更多的钱。 以下是可乐可以带来多少好处。

除此之外添加的任何东西看起来都会拖累回报。 国际股市落后。 新兴市场令人失望。 在此期间的大部分时间里，债券的回报与银行存款类似。 每一个多元化的投资组合在指数面前看起来都是一个错误。

但经过一些改造，60/40 又回来了，而且比以往任何时候都更好。

标准普尔 500 指数旨在代表广泛的市场篮子。 现在情况已不再如此：少数公司现在推动了大部分回报，因为它们推动了人工智能的建设，而其余的公司则只有少数“芯片”——双关语的意思。

与此同时，自 20 世纪 90 年代中期以来，美国上市公司的数量大约减少了一半，从接近 8,000 家减少到如今的不到 5,000 家。

过去定义指数并在发展早期上市的公司现在选择等待。 相反，它们保持私有状态——许多公司在实现曲棍球棒式增长后很久才上市，导致公共投资者追逐一艘已经离开港口的船只。

今年夏天的 SpaceX SPCX 首次公开募股是这一转变的最清晰的例证。 该公司在私人手中度过了二十多年之后，于 6 月以超过 2 万亿美元的估值上市。 这并非异常现象。 这是一个既定的模式。

自 2000 年以来，美国科技公司首次公开募股的平均年龄大约翻了一番，从大约 6 岁增加到 12 岁。 曾经需要公开市场为其下一阶段增长提供资金的公司现在不缺乏愿意为增长提供资金的私人资本，也不缺乏避免公有制带来的季度审查的理由。
